question: Should OpenClaw core provide a general agent-origin attestation mechanism for outbound HTTP requests, and if so should it be static headers, signed cryptographic attestations, a plugin/skill contract, or a ClawHub-owned integration pattern?
rationale: The request changes public identity, signing, privacy, config, skill metadata, and outbound-request semantics, so the permanent trust model and owner boundary require maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core attestation
options.body: Define a core opt-in, domain-scoped attestation model with signed/static semantics, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep attribution provider-scoped
options.body: Treat current provider attribution and provider request-header controls as the supported path, and decline general arbitrary-HTTP agent attestation for now.

options.title: Move to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Require external services to use plugin, skill, or service-level handshakes unless a missing generic core API is identified and approved.

recommendation.title: Design core attestation
recommendation.body: Define a core opt-in, domain-scoped attestation model with signed/static semantics, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the most relevant current-main provider request, attribution, and web_fetch seams that would shape a core implementation decision.
